questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship among the four Earth spheres?

options.A: They are isolated and do not exchange matter or energy
options.B: They are interacting systems through which matter and energy move continuously
options.C: Only the biosphere interacts with other spheres
options.D: Only the atmosphere and lithosphere interact

questions.explanation: The four interacting spheres are not isolated; matter and energy move continuously among them. Examples include the water cycle, volcanic eruptions and weathering.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of environmental interaction involving the hydrosphere and biosphere?
questions.explanation: Transpiration by plants (biosphere) affects atmospheric moisture (atmosphere) and is linked to the hydrosphere. Plant uptake of soil nutrients links biosphere and lithosphere; rivers transporting sediments link hydrosphere and lithosphere.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of environmental interaction involving the lithosphere and hydrosphere?

options.C: Volcanic eruptions transferring material to the atmosphere

questions.explanation: Rivers transporting sediments link the hydrosphere and lithosphere.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of environmental interaction involving the biosphere and lithosphere?
questions.explanation: Plant uptake of soil nutrients links the biosphere and lithosphere.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of environmental interaction involving the lithosphere and atmosphere?

options.A: Volcanic eruptions transferring material from the lithosphere to the atmosphere

questions.explanation: Volcanic eruptions transfer material from the lithosphere to the atmosphere.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of environmental interaction involving the atmosphere and biosphere?
questions.explanation: Transpiration by plants (biosphere) affects atmospheric moisture (atmosphere).

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of human land-use change altering habitats?
questions.explanation: Human land-use change altering habitats includes deforestation for agriculture, urban expansion and mining, among other activities.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a natural process that changes the environment?
questions.explanation: Natural processes that change the environment include weather, erosion, succession, volcanic activity and climate variability.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a human action that changes the environment?
questions.explanation: Human actions that change the environment include urbanisation, extraction, pollution, deforestation and conservation.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a conservation action that changes the environment?
questions.explanation: Conservation actions such as protecting a forest, restoring a wetland and afforestation change the environment.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: An ecosystem may be small, such as a pond, or extensive, such as a forest or ocean.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a spatial feature of an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Spatial features of an ecosystem include vegetation layers or aquatic zones.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a component of ecosystem structure?
questions.explanation: Ecosystem structure includes abiotic components; biotic components; trophic levels; food chains and food webs; and spatial features.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Major functions of an ecosystem include productivity, energy transfer, decomposition and nutrient cycling. Ecosystems also provide habitat and regulate environmental processes.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Ecosystems also provide habitat and regulate environmental processes, in addition to productivity, energy transfer, decomposition and nutrient cycling.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a consumer?
questions.explanation: Consumers include herbivores, carnivores and omnivores.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a producer?
questions.explanation: Producers include green plants, algae and photosynthetic bacteria.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a decomposer?
questions.explanation: Decomposers—especially bacteria and fungi—chemically break down dead organic matter.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a detritivore?
questions.explanation: Detritivores such as earthworms fragment dead organic matter.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an omnivore?

options.A: An organism that eats both plants and animals
options.B: An organism that eats only plants
options.C: An organism that eats only animals
options.D: An organism that produces its own food

questions.explanation: Omnivores eat both plants and animals and may occupy more than one trophic level.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a trophic level?
questions.explanation: Trophic levels are feeding positions: first level—producers; second—primary consumers; third—secondary consumers; fourth—tertiary consumers.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an ecological pyramid?
questions.explanation: Ecological pyramids show trophic levels by number of organisms, biomass or energy.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following pyramids can be inverted?
questions.explanation: Pyramids of number or biomass may be upright or inverted depending on the ecosystem. The energy pyramid is always upright.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the pyramid of numbers is correct?

options.A: It may be inverted, e.g. one tree supporting many insects
options.D: It is the same as the pyramid of biomass

questions.explanation: Pyramids of number may be inverted, e.g. one tree supporting many insects.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the pyramid of biomass is correct?

options.B: It can be inverted in some aquatic systems because phytoplankton have low standing biomass but rapid turnover
options.C: It measures the number of organisms
options.D: It is the same as the pyramid of energy

questions.explanation: Biomass pyramids can be inverted in some aquatic systems because phytoplankton have low standing biomass but rapid turnover.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the pyramid of energy is correct?

options.B: It is always upright because usable energy decreases at each transfer
options.C: It measures the number of organisms

questions.explanation: Pyramids of energy are always upright because usable energy decreases at each transfer; energy is lost as heat and through metabolism.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about energy flow in ecosystems is correct?

options.B: Energy flows one way and requires continual input
options.C: Energy is stored permanently in biomass
options.D: Energy flows in both directions between trophic levels

questions.explanation: Energy flow is one-way and requires continual input; unlike nutrients, energy is not recycled.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about ecological succession is correct?

options.A: It is the gradual change in species composition and community structure over time
options.B: It is the one-way flow of energy
options.C: It is the cycling of nutrients
options.D: It is the process of photosynthesis

questions.explanation: Ecological succession is the gradual change in species composition and community structure over time.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a disturbance that can lead to secondary succession?
questions.explanation: Secondary succession follows disturbance such as fire, cultivation or storm where soil, seeds or roots may remain.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a pioneer species?

options.A: Species that first colonise a newly available or disturbed habitat
options.B: Species that appear only in climax communities

questions.explanation: Pioneer species are early colonisers of a newly available or disturbed habitat.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about climax communities is correct?

options.A: A climax community is always permanent
options.B: Modern ecology recognises that disturbances and environmental change can prevent a single permanent climax
options.C: A climax community is the first species to colonise an area
options.D: A climax community has no species diversity

questions.explanation: A climax community is the relatively persistent late-successional community under prevailing conditions; modern ecology recognises that disturbances and environmental change can prevent a single permanent climax.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a level of biodiversity?
questions.explanation: Biodiversity includes diversity within species (genetic), between species (species) and of ecosystems (ecosystem).

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of genetic diversity?

options.A: Variation in genes within a species or population
options.B: The variety and relative abundance of species
options.C: The variety of habitats, communities and ecological processes

questions.explanation: Genetic diversity is variation in genes within a species or population.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of species diversity?

options.A: Variation in genes within a species
options.B: The variety and relative abundance of species
options.C: The variety of habitats, communities and ecological processes

questions.explanation: Species diversity concerns the variety and relative abundance of species.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of ecosystem diversity?

options.A: Variation in genes within a species
options.B: The variety and relative abundance of species
options.C: The variety of habitats, communities and ecological processes in a region

questions.explanation: Ecosystem diversity is the variety of habitats, communities and ecological processes in a region.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a biodiversity hotspot that includes parts of India?
questions.explanation: Four global hotspots include parts of India: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, and Sundaland.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about hotspot boundaries is correct?

options.A: Hotspot boundaries are identical to political boundaries
options.B: Hotspot boundaries are biogeographic, not identical to political boundaries
options.C: Hotspot boundaries are the same as protected area boundaries
options.D: Hotspot boundaries are the same as Ramsar site boundaries

questions.explanation: Hotspot boundaries are biogeographic, not identical to political boundaries.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about endemic species is correct?

options.A: Endemism automatically means a species is threatened
options.B: Endemism does not automatically mean a species is threatened
options.C: Endemic species are found all over the world

questions.explanation: Endemism does not automatically mean a species is threatened.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an IUCN Red List category?
questions.explanation: IUCN Red List categories include Extinct (EX), Extinct in the Wild (EW), Critically Endangered (CR), Endangered (EN), Vulnerable (VU), Near Threatened (NT), Least Concern (LC), Data Deficient (DD) and Not Evaluated (NE).

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an invasive alien species in India?
questions.explanation: Examples in India include water hyacinth, Lantana camara and Prosopis juliflora in affected landscapes.

questions.subject: Environmental Geography and Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a major threat to biodiversity?
questions.explanation: Major threats include illegal wildlife trade, disease and unsustainable land- and water-use change, among others.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of in-situ conservation?
questions.explanation: In-situ conservation examples include national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, conservation reserves, community reserves and biosphere reserves.
